page: Microsoft Azure M64ms_v2 is a memory-optimized instance from the MSMediumMemoryv2 family, engineered for extremely RAM-dense enterprise workloads. The virtual machine runs on Microsoft Hyper-V virtualization and is powered by an x86_64 Intel processor. It provides 64 dedicated vCPUs alongside 1792.0 GB of system memory, which establishes an expansive memory footprint yielding 28.0 GB of RAM per vCPU.

Hardware architecture for the M64ms_v2 focuses strictly on CPU and RAM density, omitting dedicated hardware accelerators such as GPUs. Additionally, the instance provides no local ephemeral storage out of the box, relying instead on network-attached remote storage solutions like Azure Premium Storage. The environment also includes zero complimentary public IPv4 addresses, necessitating standard Azure virtual networking components for external routing.

From a cost-efficiency and architecture tradeoff perspective, the M64ms_v2 concentrates resources entirely on massive memory allocation rather than local I/O performance or graphics compute. Because it provides no integrated local disk, persistent workloads must account for the latency and throughput characteristics of external storage. The instance serves environments with substantial memory-retention requirements, making it suited for large-scale in-memory databases, SAP HANA deployments, massive data warehousing caches, and high-footprint enterprise analytics engines.

Operating without complimentary public IPv4 addresses, the instance is engineered to handle resource-heavy operations where immense RAM capacity is the critical requirement. Given its high RAM-to-vCPU ratio, the M64ms_v2 is suited for large in-memory database engines, SAP HANA systems, extensive data caching, and enterprise-grade in-memory analytics workloads.
